I am 55 years old and I have farmed my 7 mu in Quzhou County for 35 years. I only finished primary school. I learned everything from my father and from watching my neighbors. My wife works with me, and my son does construction in Shijiazhuang and sends some money home. I have a well for irrigation.

For winter wheat, I do what I did last year. In October, I rotary till all 7 mu. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer in town — about 12 kg per mu. Before sowing, I spread one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. The bag says 15-15-15. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I topdress with 30 kg of urea per mu. Two years ago I used only 15 kg of urea to save money, and my yield dropped badly. My neighbor Wang used his normal amount and his wheat was much greener. I lost more than 100 jin per mu. So now I make sure to put enough. I would rather waste some fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. I irrigate three times: once before winter freeze, once in April at jointing, and once in May at heading. I spray three times — herbicide after sowing, and two more times in spring for aphids and rust. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

For summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. There is no time to plow. I hire the no-till planter that drills through the wheat straw. Everyone uses it now. I buy hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu. I put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu when planting. Then in late July, when the maize is knee-high, I side-dress with 20 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once when the plants are tasseling, and once at flowering if it is dry. I spray twice: herbicide at sowing, and once in August for corn borer. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

My fertilizer costs about 220 yuan per mu for wheat and 190 yuan for maize. It is a big expense. But a bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just money.
